ef9748393af233c9: The three combat styles a squad can take
992e3fec1e41dec5: Formation{a=00} lets a squad of two or three units change how it lines up, changing its combat ability with it.{/a}
fb8383fadb8e203f: There are three, and you can switch freely until the squad ends its action.
0875f8b1c4ef8ce4: The enemy uses them too, so learn what each does and which beats which.
e87ddf4431cb37e5: The basic form, and the only one with Tri Charge
c19ed78e43779d1f: The leader takes point, members in single file behind. Squads always deploy this way. Its great advantage is that it alone can use {a=0e}Tri Charge{/a}, a pseudo-combination attack.
3d4764bc9551d2d0: Members join no attack but Tri Charge; in exchange the leader shields them, so they gain a defense bonus. Only Sup Defend protects the leader, so pick a tough unit that will not be shot down.

de90ae36e29071ba: Members close up in front. The squad can hit one unit of the enemy squad with a squad attack, then have the leader attack it too. If any unit in the squad has a barrier, {a=0e}Wide Barrier{/a} applies it to the whole squad.
3e437a9ba2c5c6d5: Ideal for concentrating on one enemy, but fragile once the members are targeted. For leader, pick a unit whose leader effect cuts damage or boosts barriers.
